business_scope.primary_industry_name: Remote Desktop Access and Unattended Machine Telemetry Software

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of the People's Republic of China on Anti-Money Laundering (as amended), Counter-Terrorism Law of the People's Republic of China, PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3 - Measures for the Administration of Beneficial Owner Information of Legal Persons and Other Organizations (effective November 1, 2024), PRC Company Law (2023 revision), PRC Foreign Investment Law, Administrative Measures for Enterprise Name Registration, and PBOC Customer Due Diligence Rules.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / Company Registration Certificate of the Taiwan joint venture partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Company Registration Authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Non-Hague consular legalization path (mutually exclusive with Apostille; never chained): Taiwan notary public certification -> Taiwan District Court notary office authentication -> Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF) certification -> Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits (ARATS) verification in Mainland China -> PRC notarized Chinese translation submitted to SAMR.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of the Taiwan joint venture partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Non-Hague consular legalization path: MOEA certificate -> Taiwan notary certification -> SEF/ARATS verification; no Apostille is competent for Taiwan-origin documents.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution of the Taiwan investor authorizing the formation of the Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture and granting Power of Attorney to the local representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the Taiwan investor, duly notarized
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Non-Hague consular legalization path (Taiwan): original board resolution notarized before Taiwan notary -> SEF certification -> ARATS verification -> Chinese translation with notarial attestation; if the investor were in a Hague Convention state, the exclusive alternative would be notarization + Apostille, never both paths.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association and Joint Venture Contract of the PRC Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: All joint venture parties signed before a licensed PRC notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For PRC/Taiwan execution: Chinese notarial certificate covers signatures and legalization; for any foreign investor in a Hague state, Apostille is obtained separately and exclusively for that foreign party's execution pages; Taiwan execution pages must follow SEF/ARATS verification; the two authentication routes are parallel and are never sequentially combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the Taiwan investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan commercial bank (branch manager or authorized officer)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Non-Hague consular legalization path: bank officer signature and corporate seal certified by Taiwan notary -> SEF/ARATS verification; no Apostille applicable to Taiwan; if issued by a Hague-state bank, notary + Apostille only.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Registration of the PRC Foreign-Invested Enterprise (post-incorporation evidence bundle)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: SAMR or its authorized local Market Supervision Administration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: PRC domestic document, no foreign legalization or Apostille required; the registered copy obtained from SAMR is the final proof filed for tax and bank account opening.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, legal representatives, ultimate beneficial owners, and authorized signatories against PRC Ministry of Public Security and Ministry of Foreign Affairs sanctions lists, UN Security Council Consolidated Lists, OFAC SDN and non-SDN sanctions lists, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, and domestic PEP databases before incorporation. Enhanced due diligence is required for politically exposed persons, their family members and close associates; each natural person must undergo continuous sanctions list matching, source-of-funds verification, negative news checks, and adverse media review; hit-management and asset freeze obligations are triggered immediately under PRC AML and Counter-Terrorism Law, with filings to PBOC and SAMR Order No. 3 beneficial-owner register.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Registration and Name Clearance Online System (National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered name must be in Simplified Chinese using the four-tier statutory structure: [administrative division] + [trade name] + [industry or business characteristic] + [organizational form]. A Taiwan investor's company name must be transliterated into Simplified Chinese pinyin for use in the JV trade name; traditional Chinese characters and foreign scripts are not accepted in the registered corporate name. Latin letters, Arabic numerals, and hyphens are permitted only in a separately filed English name or as strictly limited elements of the trade name; all official correspondence and tax invoices must use the Chinese registered name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may file a written appeal with the same SAMR registration authority within 15 working days, attaching the official rejection notice, the proposed name, revised alternatives, and a legal memorandum substantiating compliance with the four-tier naming rules. If the registry sustains the rejection, the applicant may apply for administrative reconsideration to the next-higher market supervision authority or to the relevant people's government within 60 days, and may initiate administrative litigation before a people's court within 6 months from the reconsideration decision unless a longer period is otherwise prescribed. Re-application with a new name is permitted at any time through the online portal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office or commercial mailbox address is rejected by Chinese tax authorities and major corporate banks as the sole registered address for a Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture engaged in remote screen-share software development. SAMR and the tax authority require a lawful physical business premise in the registered district; although incubator or co-working space addresses may be accepted when the operator is recognized and a genuine lease exists, banks still perform on-site verification and will decline account opening if the office appears empty, lacks a corporate nameplate, or has no verifiable staff. Virtual-office-only arrangements also create material annual-report, payroll, VAT invoice, and foreign-exchange-remittance compliance failures under PBOC rules.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: registered address signage, lease or property ownership certificate, utility bills, employee attendance, payroll records, social security contributions, accounting books, bank statements, corporate seal custody log, IT hardware, and remote-access servers. Quantified risk: approximately 60% probability of an unannounced SAMR or municipal tax inspection during the first 12 months if a virtual-office/mailbox address is used; approximately 25-30% probability for a physically staffed and fully documented office with installed equipment.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) / local Market Supervision Administration
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee tariff: zero official government registration fee under the current PRC fee-reduction policy; any attorney preparation fee is separate.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO information filing and update obligation under PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: People's Bank of China and State Administration for Market Regulation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory filing, no official government fee; registration-threshold reporting must be made within 30 days after incorporation.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Taiwan investor document notarization and SEF/ARATS cross-strait authentication
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Taiwan notary public, Taiwan District Court notary office, Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF), Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits (ARATS)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed official charges plus prevailing market notarial tariffs for cross-strait certificate verification.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Chinese translation and notarial attestation of Taiwan and English corporate documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed PRC translation company and PRC notary public
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate per page (Approx. USD 0.50-1.50 per word equivalent) plus notarial certification fee.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of Joint Venture Contract, Articles of Association, board resolutions, and shareholder agreements
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External PRC law firm (mandatory legal sign-off for Sino-Foreign JV)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for cross-border technology JV formation with Taiwan shareholder: 8-15 hours at firm rates.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office physical lease deposit and first-year occupancy contribution (shared office or incubator)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Commercial landlord, business incubator, or registered-address service provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rent benchmarks for registered address and minimum physical desking space in tier-1 Chinese cities.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate seal engraving and legalization (company seal, financial seal, contract seal, legal representative seal)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market tariff per seal per city, including chip-based public security filing.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/KYC screening database access, PEP and sanctions list run, and UBO verification report
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Commercial due-diligence data provider (e.g., identity verification and sanctions-screening platform)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: One-time project benchmark and per-record screening fee for the Taiwan investor and each UBO/PEP subject.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Post-incorporation SAMR copy, tax registration, social insurance registration, and bank account opening coordination
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: PRC corporate service agent / licensed intermediary
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for administrative travel and filing coordination in the target district.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act (Act), R.O.C.; in particular Articles 387, 388, 393 and 438; Act Governing Relations between the People of the Taiwan Area and the Mainland Area, Article 73; Regulations Governing Investment in Taiwan by Mainland-Area Investors; Regulations Governing Permission of Investment of Foreign Nationals insofar as non-mainland shareholders participate; Civil Code Article 25 for juristic person capacity when compatible.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, R.O.C. (MOEA), Department of Commercial Affairs; Investment Commission of MOEA for mainland China investment permit; MOEA One-Stop Online Business Registration system and the central company register portal maintained by the R.O.C. Commerce Development and research center.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Company Limited by Shares under Article 387 of the Taiwan Company Act, accompanied by the Investment Permit of the Investment Commission, capital verification report, Articles of Incorporation, first board resolution minutes, and registered office lease or letter of consent.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None under the Taiwan Company Act: there is no statutory minimum paid-up capital for a company limited by shares. Nevertheless, the full authorized capital must be subscribed, and 100% of subscribed cash capital must be paid into a NT$ designated bank capital account in Taiwan before the statutory registration application is filed. A licensed Taiwan CPA must issue a capital verification report confirming the cash deposit. Where a mainland China investor participates, the capital remittance must be from the approved mainland investment project and must remain blocked from operational disbursement until the Certificate of Incorporation is issued and the company bank account mandate is perfected. A zero-share or shell-capital structure cannot satisfy the capital verification rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME]

RESOLVED, that the Company, having been provisionally formed by the founding shareholders of this Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture Limited Company under the Taiwan Company Act, hereby ratifies, adopts and approves in their entirety the final Articles of Incorporation appended to this board package. The board records its determination that the lawful object of the Company is confined to the approved business scope: computer programming, remote desktop access and unattended machine telemetry software, Internet of Things data processing, and related professional consulting services under ISIC 6201 and NAICS 511210, as filed with the Ministry of Economic Affairs, and that the Company shall not engage in physical manufacturing, chemical processing, warehousing, or assembly without a further board resolution and the necessary industrial and environmental licences.

RESOLVED, that the registered share capital of the Company is fixed at NT$[●], divided into [●] ordinary shares of NT$[●] each, and that the initial share subscription schedule is hereby confirmed. Each founding shareholder shall pay its subscription in cash in full into the Company capital subscription account before statutory registration. The directors are directed to engage a licensed certified public accountant to verify all capital payments and to prepare the capital verification report required by the competent registry and the Investment Commission.

RESOLVED, that the Company adopts [bank name and branch] as its principal banker and authorizes the opening of a New Taiwan Dollar demand deposit account, a foreign currency account, and any e-banking or treasury facility required for the Company operation. The Chairman, the President, and the Chief Financial Officer, or any two of them acting jointly, are authorized to execute account opening documents, sign cheques and transfer instructions, approve wire transfers, conclude foreign exchange contracts, appoint alternates, and liaise with payment processors such as Stripe and Paddle; provided that no disbursement shall be made from the capital subscription account until the Certificate of Incorporation is issued.

RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company is fixed at [address of registered office in Taiwan]. The directors are authorized to execute or ratify the lease or letter of consent, to display the statutory company name, and to keep the corporate seal, minute books, share register, financial records and statutory filings at that office.

RESOLVED, that the following persons are appointed as statutory officers and representatives: [name] as Chairman and Representative Director; [name] as President and General Manager; [name] as Company Secretary and Compliance Officer; and [name] as Chief Financial Officer. Each appointee accepts office and undertakes to discharge the duties imposed by the Taiwan Company Act and by applicable AML/CFT and personal data protection obligations affecting the Company software subscription and remote telemetry services.

FURTHER RESOLVED, that the officers are authorized to file the incorporation application, obtain the business tax uniform number, register as an employer with labor insurance and national health insurance authorities, open merchant accounts with payment processors, execute vendor and customer agreements, appoint legal counsel and CPAs, and take any other lawful ancillary steps necessary to commence business. This resolution may be reproduced, notarized and authenticated as required. Adopted by unanimous consent of the directors on [date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Pre-Approval and Business Scope Clearance at MOEA One-Stop Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, R.O.C., Department of Commercial Affairs via the One-Stop Online Business Registration and the national company name and business scope checking system.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and file the company name and business scope pre-approval application through the MOEA One-Stop Service. Select a Chinese company name appropriate to the limited company structure and choose the approved Taiwan Standard Industrial Classification code equivalent to ISIC 6201 computer programming and information services, with an English name supporting remote desktop access, unattended machine telemetry software and Internet of Things data processing. Ensure the name is not identical or confusingly similar to existing trade names, does not contain prohibited or misleading words, and is consistent with the business scope that the Investment Commission is expected to approve. Pay the name-check fee, download the name reservation certificate, and note the priority date and validity period; any change in the investment plan that affects the proposed name or scope requires a fresh pre-approval before further steps are taken.
required_dossiers: Proposed Chinese company name and business scope application (online form)
Passport or National ID of each founding shareholder and authorized agent
Company name and business scope checking fee payment receipt
Power of attorney executed in favor of a Taiwan-licensed formation agent
English name and ISIC 6201/NAICS 511210 supporting business description
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or suspended, respond to the MOEA within seven calendar days, correct the conflicting name or business scope and resubmit. If refusal is issued, file an administrative appeal under the Administrative Remedy Procedures or submit a fresh application with revised name and scope; no construction step should occur pending resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Mainland Investor Investment Permit from the Investment Commission of MOEA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs, R.O.C., online application portal and physical counter in Taipei.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Since the equity joint venture includes a mainland China investor, submit the mainland investment permit application before any Taiwan company registration proceeds. Provide the detailed investment plan, ownership chart, proof of lawful mainland business, latest audited financial statements, source of funds declaration, proposed Taiwan entity capital structure, and Articles of Incorporation. Explain the ISIC 6201 remote desktop and unattended machine telemetry business, including data flow routing, personal data protection, and cross-border telemetry compliance. The Investment Commission will issue a permit containing the approved capital amount, shareholding ratio, and restricted business scope. Do not remit capital or file the statutory company registration before the permit is issued. If the mainland investor is a public company or holds sensitive technology, a negative list review and additional security assessment may apply.
required_dossiers: Investment Commission Mainland-Area Investor investment application (Form 1)
Notarized copy of the mainland investor business license or corporate registration certificate
Audited financial statements of the mainland investor for the latest two years
Ultimate beneficial ownership chart and identity statements
Investment plan with projected revenue, headcount and Taiwan registered office address
Proposed Articles of Incorporation and board resolution of the mainland investor approving the joint venture
Power of attorney appointing a Taiwan attorney or formation agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to Investment Commission comments within thirty calendar days; provide notarized translations or supplemental bank references if requested. If the permit is denied, the investor may request administrative reconsideration before the Executive Yuan, or restructure the joint venture to reduce mainland ownership below the regulatory threshold, or receive the Investment Commission opinion and reapply after curing the identified defect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Remittance, Blocked Capital Account Opening and CPA Capital Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Designated Foreign Exchange Bank in Taiwan supervised by the Central Bank of the R.O.C., and a licensed Taiwan certified public accountant.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Investment Commission permit, open a capital subscription account at a designated bank in Taiwan and remit the approved capital in NT$ or foreign currency converted to NT$. The bank will issue a Foreign Exchange Transaction Certificate showing the remitter, amount and purpose. Funds must remain segregated in the capital account and shall not be withdrawn for operational expenses until the statutory registration is complete and the certificate of incorporation is issued. Engage a licensed Taiwan CPA to examine the receipt, subscriber list, bank passbook and Investment Commission permit. The CPA must issue a capital verification report confirming that all subscribed capital has been physically paid, that no subscriber has withdrawn funds, and that the share allocation matches the approved investment permit. This report must be dated no earlier than fifteen days before the registration submission.
required_dossiers: Investment Commission approval letter and approved capital schedule
Board resolution authorizing bank account opening and signatories
Foreign exchange transaction certificate from the designated bank
Capital remittance instructions and SWIFT/telex proof
List of founding shareholders and exact subscription amounts
CPA engagement letter and capital verification work papers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank blocks or queries the inward remittance, provide a copy of the Investment Commission permit and the mainland investor certificate and ask the bank to issue a corrected foreign exchange certificate. If the CPA raises source-of-funds concerns, submit additional bank statements, dividend invoices, audited financial statements and affidavits; if the bank refuses the account mandate, select an alternate designated bank and file a notice of change with the Investment Commission before proceeding.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Corporate Registration with MOEA Department of Commercial Affairs
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, R.O.C., Department of Commercial Affairs, through the Company Registration online service.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the statutory incorporation application within fifteen days from the conclusion of the incorporating meeting, unless the Registrar accepts a later filing. Attach the fully executed Articles of Incorporation, incorporation meeting minutes, first board resolution, capital verification report, Investment Commission permit, bank capital deposit certificate, registered office consent or lease, valid identification of directors and officers, company seal specimens and share register. The Registrar will examine the application under Article 388 of the Company Act, verify that the paid-up capital has been released into the blocked capital account, that the business scope is lawful, and that all mandatory filings are consistent. Upon acceptance, the Ministry of Economic Affairs issues the Certificate of Incorporation and the business tax uniform number is assigned. After issuance, the company must record the company seal and open its operational bank accounts before releasing the blocked capital.
required_dossiers: Company registration application form (Article 387)
CPA capital verification report
Original or notarized Articles of Incorporation
Minutes of the incorporating meeting and first board resolution
Investment Commission Mainland Investment Permit
Bank capital deposit certificate or passbook
Certificate of registered office consent and landlord title deed or lease
Valid IDs and appointment consents of directors, chairman, supervisors and officers
Company seal specimen and authorized signatures
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a correction notice, the applicant has fifteen calendar days to supplement or amend the application; repeated failure may attract an administrative refusal. If refusal occurs, the applicant may file an administrative appeal, redo the faulty capital verification, or amend the articles and resubmit; failing which, a new incorporation application with a fresh capital verification report is required. Any material deviation from the Investment Commission permit requires prior re-approval by the Investment Commission before registration can cure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Tax, Labor, National Health Insurance and Social Compliance Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Administration of the Ministry of Finance, R.O.C., local district tax office, Bureau of Labor Insurance, and National Health Insurance Administration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within fifteen days of the Certificate of Incorporation, verify the automatic tax registration and obtain the official business tax uniform invoice number; where e-invoices are required, apply for e-invoice encoding and issue settings. Register as an employer with the labor insurance, labor pension and national health insurance authorities, and file the employee payroll and appointment records. Confirm whether the remote desktop and unattended telemetry software qualifies for export service zero-rating, and retain customer contracts and technical service descriptions because the tax authority may query cross-border service revenue. Keep board minutes, share register and AML/CFT risk assessments at the registered office, and ensure that payment processor contracts with Stripe and Paddle are supported by a proper corporate bank account, merchant registration and compliance policies for data processing under Taiwan personal data protection law.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and uniform business tax number notice
Company seal card and responsible person identification
Business premises lease and occupancy certificate
Final Articles of Incorporation and first board resolution
Employer labor insurance and labor pension registration forms
National health insurance employer registration form
E-invoice and VAT registration application where applicable
Payment processor underwriting information and AML questionnaire
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office issues a query, respond within fourteen days with lease, revenue projection and explanation of software service export. If the labor insurance office finds missing employees, submit the corrected payroll and pay any underestimate within fifteen days. If the district tax office refuses e-invoice issuance because of incomplete premises evidence, relocate the registered office or provide electricity bill and landlord certification and re-file; no operational software service should be sold before the tax registration is fully effective unless under a compliance risk treatment approved by the district office.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - Pure digital software and telemetry services under ISIC 6201 require no industrial licensing board because the company performs no physical manufacturing, assembly, chemical processing, or warehousing. If a data center or hardware logistics hub is later added, the Industrial Development Administration, MOEA, and the local municipal public works authority would become competent.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - No industrial operating permit, factory registration certificate, assembly permit, chemical storage permit, or warehouse license is required for remote desktop access and unattended machine telemetry software. The company only requires ordinary commercial registration, tax registration, and personal data protection compliance for the SaaS and IoT data services.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Administration of the Executive Yuan, Taiwan; local municipal environmental protection bureau would become competent only if physical construction, manufacturing, or a large data center were introduced.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Not Applicable. The ISIC 6201 software operation presents no trigger for a Class A full EIA report, Class B project EIA, or Class C environmental registration because no construction, production, chemical handling, wastewater discharge, hazardous waste generation, or significant air emission is involved. Minor office decoration is below the EIA screening threshold.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: None applicable for the software operation: wastewater 0 m3/day, VOC emissions 0 kg/hr, hazardous waste 0 t/yr from the core ISIC 6201 activity. Electronic waste from replaced office IT equipment must be handled through registered recycling vendors, and any cloud infrastructure is the responsibility of third-party hosting providers. If a physical data center is added, the company must then comply with central Taiwan greenhouse gas, standby power generator, and electronic waste regulations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for manufacturing fire permits; however, because the company will occupy a Taiwan office, the building must maintain a valid fire safety equipment inspection certificate under the Fire Services Act if the premises are classified as a public or non-residential building. The employer must register occupational safety and health arrangements covering emergency exits, fire extinguishers, first-aid stations, electrical safety, lighting, and worker accident insurance; no special civil defense license is required for pure software and remote support operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance, Tax Administration, Republic of China (Taiwan), acting through the applicable regional National Taxation Bureau; electronic filings are submitted through the MOF e-Filing (Tax E-Net) portal and the Cloud Invoice Integration Service Platform for uniform invoice/e-invoice data.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture is first incorporated as a Taiwan limited company, with foreign investors obtaining investment approval from the Investment Commission of the Ministry of Economic Affairs. After incorporation, the company must file business tax registration with the regional National Taxation Bureau using the statutory application package, company registration certificate, articles of incorporation, legal representative and shareholder identity documents, business premise proof, and accounting/book records; the Bureau will issue the eight-digit Business Administration Number that functions as the TIN and VAT registration number. For foreign non-resident corporate shareholders, certified corporate existence documents, board resolutions, powers of attorney naming a Taiwan resident tax agent, and evidence of inward capital remittance must be submitted, translated and notarized as required. A non-resident entity selling digital services solely to Taiwan B2C customers may instead apply for simplified cross-border electronic service provider registration through the Ministry of Finance online registration mechanism; if it does not register, a Taiwan B2B customer must self-assess the 5% VAT by reverse charge.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None; Taiwan does not have a check-the-box partnership or hybrid election. A limited joint venture is taxed at entity level under the Income Tax Act, and no flow-through or hybrid mismatch election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: A Taiwan-established joint venture has no general monetary turnover threshold and must register before starting taxable business. A non-resident cross-border electronic service provider selling digital services to Taiwan individuals must register if annual B2C turnover exceeds TWD 480,000; below that threshold registration is optional, and B2B supplies by an unregistered foreign provider are subject to reverse-charge VAT by the Taiwan buyer.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Taiwan mandates the Uniform Invoice system. Businesses that use electronic invoices must transmit invoice data to the Ministry of Finance Cloud Invoice Integration Service Platform via the certified Turnkey gateway or an API connector, submit the bimonthly business tax return by the 15th day of the month following the two-month reporting period, and retain invoice issuance and payment records. The regime is not an ex-ante real-time fiscal clearance model, but it combines serialized uniform invoice numbers, printed random four-digit anti-counterfeit validation codes, return/payment cross-matching, and periodic tax authority audits to deter fraud.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available under Article 7 of the Value-added and Non-value-added Business Tax Act where export goods are actually dispatched from Taiwan customs or where services, including remote screen-share and IoT telemetry software, are sold to non-resident customers and are performed/used entirely outside Taiwan. For services, the export contract, delivery/usage evidence, and receipt of consideration in foreign currency are required; the zero-rated turnover must be stated separately on the uniform invoice and included as zero-rated export turnover in the bimonthly business tax return. Input VAT attributable to such exports may be carried forward or refunded.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (export declaration form) released by Taiwan Customs
Commercial invoice and, where applicable, zero-rated uniform invoice
Bill of lading (ocean) or air waybill (air cargo)
Foreign exchange inward remittance certificate (FIRC) or bank foreign exchange declaration form evidencing collection from the foreign buyer
Export service contract and performance evidence (service logs, telemetry access records, or delivery reports) demonstrating offshore use for remote software and IoT services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The regional National Taxation Bureau audits zero-rated export documentation on a transactional basis. If documentation is incomplete, forged, or shows the service was actually used in Taiwan, the tax authority will reclassify the sale as taxable, issue a deficiency assessment plus interest, and impose administrative penalties up to five times the evaded business tax, with possible suspension of business. Fraudulent export documentation or false foreign-exchange repatriation evidence may additionally trigger criminal tax-evasion liability and disqualify the taxpayer from simplified cross-border registration and export-refund incentives.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan) (CBC); for mainland China sourced outbound flows, the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) of the People's Republic of China must also approve and file the PRC parent's outbound investment.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Taiwan operates a managed floating exchange-rate regime in which the Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan) regulates the interbank FX market. The New Taiwan Dollar is freely convertible for current-account purposes; ordinary receipts from software licensing, telemetry subscription, technical support, royalties and third-party payment settlement can be processed through authorized FX banks under the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act without prior central-bank approval, but each transaction requires a CBC foreign-exchange declaration and supporting commercial documentation. Capital-account transactions are controlled: inbound equity investment from a mainland Chinese shareholder requires prior MOEA Investment Commission clearance, SAFE outbound-investment registration, and a CBC settlement declaration before the offshore remittance is booked as paid-in capital. No general surrender requirement applies in normal times, so export proceeds may be retained in foreign-currency deposit accounts or converted to TWD at the prevailing market rate. Profit remittance to the PRC parent will be treated as a capital-account dividend outflow and requires audited financial statements, tax clearance, board dividend minutes, joint-venture contract provisions and a validated outward remittance declaration. Direct TWD/RMB clearing is limited; cross-strait treasury flows are preferentially cleared in USD or CNH via Hong Kong.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: In normal operations Taiwan does not impose a mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts; the CBC has removed the old 100% surrender rule. Exporters must repatriate and collect the proceeds through an authorized FX bank within the 180-day settlement window measured from the date of export customs declaration, unless an extension is granted for service exports, and then either deposit the funds in a foreign-currency account or settle to TWD at the bank's posted rate. A zero-percent conversion ratio applies in ordinary circumstances; if the CBC exercises its emergency balance-of-payments powers, it can require forced conversion of specific export proceeds within the timelines stated in the emergency notice, but this has not been enacted in the current regulatory environment.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (TWD/USD) and Basic Operational Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: Low, not viable as the primary corporate treasury bank. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise, Revolut, Airwallex and Stripe Treasury do not hold a Taiwan electronic-payment institution license under the Financial Supervisory Commission Act on Electronic Payment Institutions, and they are not authorized foreign-exchange banks under the CBC. They cannot provide statutory capital escrow, central-bank reporting, company capital verification or TWD settlement services for a Taiwan-registered joint venture. They may be used only as ancillary receivable-collection facilitators through regulated local payment partners for software subscription revenue, never for statutory capital, profit repatriation or treasury concentration.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical in-branch KYC interview is mandatory for at least one statutory director and one beneficial owner of the Taiwan JV; remote consular proxy opening is generally not accepted for the initial account relationship. Mainland Chinese shareholders and directors must present a valid Taiwan entry permit, identity documents, corporate establishment certificates and board resolutions. A notarized power of attorney executed at a Taiwan overseas representative office may allow additional non-resident signatories to be added, but the CBC and bank compliance committees normally require the responsible domestic director or local general manager to appear once in the branch before the account can be activated.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-strait UBO opacity: the PRC parent company controls a Taiwan JV and the shareholding chain is not visible in CBC/FSC registries, triggering heightened CDD, sanctions and round-tripping risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the MOEA Investment Commission mainland-investment approval letter; SAFE outbound-investment filing certificate from the PRC parent; a certified UBO declaration covering the complete ownership chain to natural persons; notarized articles of incorporation; board resolution approving account opening; passport and Taiwan entry permit copies of all directors; source-of-wealth documentation such as audited financial statements and bank reference letters from the PRC parent's main bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Intangible substance: the entity is a remote screen-share/IoT software company with a virtual registered office, no apparent local staff and no physical operations, creating a shell-company profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a current registered-office lease with rent receipts and utility bills; office photographs; local payroll, labor insurance and national health insurance records for Taiwan employees; director's local residence tax documents; audited or accountant-reviewed interim financial statements; invoices issued to customers; historical bank statements showing income and operating expenses; and a substance narrative mapping product development, customer support, data hosting and sales functions to Taiwan.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Remote-support and unattended-telemetry software can be abused for unauthorized network access, industrial data exfiltration or deployment to sanctioned end-users, which is an AML/export-control concern despite the low financial-risk tier.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a formal end-user and reseller due-diligence policy; an acceptable-use policy; a privacy policy and EULA; third-party penetration test report and ISO/IEC 27001 certificate; OFAC/UK/EU sanctions screening logs with redactions only for personal data; an export-control classification memorandum for the software; a no-go jurisdiction list; customer onboarding records showing the physical location of screen-share sessions and device telemetry; and a written commitment to block access from prohibited jurisdictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection may be sourced from uncleared mainland intermediaries or from personal bank accounts instead of the named PRC corporate shareholder, creating provenance failure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supply a bank-to-bank SWIFT MT103 showing the remitter as the exact named PRC shareholder; the MOEA Investment Commission approval; the SAFE ODI registration; a capital verification report from a Taiwan-certified CPA after receipt; the Taiwan CBC foreign-exchange declaration receipt; the remitter's bank statement showing the funds are corporate operating cash flows, not individual deposits; the joint-venture capital contribution schedule; and the board resolution authoring the capital increase.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Obtain MOEA Investment Commission investment approval and PRC SAFE outbound-investment registration before any remittance. Route the capital injection as a bank-to-bank SWIFT MT103 from the named PRC corporate shareholder through its PRC bank to the Taiwan entity's capital escrow account at Bank of Taiwan or Mega International Commercial Bank. The receiving Taiwan bank will require the remitter to use the CBC inward-remittance declaration category for foreign direct investment, not trade payment; include a clear reference in SWIFT field 70 such as DIRECT EQUITY SUBSCRIPTION PER BOARD RESOLUTION AND MOEAIC APPROVAL. Upon receipt, freeze TWD/USD in the escrow account until the CPA issues the capital verification report and the Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs files the paid-in capital registration. Never use Stripe, Paddle or any EMI to inject capital, because those rails cannot provide CBC reporting or capital verification evidence.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SWIFT MT103 for software licensing royalties, cloud infrastructure fees, overseas subcontractors, dividends and ordinary operational disbursements. For physical IoT hardware resale, use an irrevocable at-sight commercial letter of credit via SWIFT MT700/MT710 with a Taiwan negotiating bank; for smaller recurring trade settlements, documentary collections D/P or D/A are acceptable but carry higher clearing risk. Every outbound trade payment must be supported by an underlying invoice, contract, import declaration or service agreement and must be reported to the CBC through the settling Taiwan bank. Cross-strait payments to the PRC parent should be routed in USD or CNH, not TWD, and must clear through a permitted offshore CNY clearing bank such as a Hong Kong clearing bank or a Taiwan authorized FX bank with offshore CNY capability.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable outright USD/TWD forward contracts, limited to documented forecasted software subscriptions, royalty receivables and operational payables with genuine exposure.
FX swaps between TWD and USD to manage liquidity mismatches between capital injection, operating costs and dividend distribution dates.
Cross-currency swaps under ISDA for long-term foreign-currency financing or intercompany loan exposures, with CBC reporting and real-exposure documentation.

Restricted boundary: onshore Taiwan-resident corporate entities are generally not permitted to use non-deliverable forward NDF contracts for speculative purposes; NDFs are confined to non-resident counterparties, so the JV should rely on deliverable forwards and prohibited from leveraged FX option trades.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Settlement Return (Form 15) and related-party transaction disclosure
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Finance – National Taxation Bureau of the jurisdiction in which the JV is registered
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year accounting period, file on or before 31 May of the following year; an application-based extension may be available until 30 June if the company applies before the original due date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a 3% additional tax for each two-week period of delay, capped at 9%, plus statutory interest on the outstanding amount; inaccuracies/reporting omissions can attract up to three times the undercharged tax; persistent non-filing and cessation of business can lead to MOEA administrative dissolution under Company Act Article 10.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Bi-monthly Business Tax (VAT) Return and Unified Invoice usage report (six filing periods per year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Finance – National Taxation Bureau of the jurisdiction in which the JV is registered
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due by the 15th day of the month following each two-month period: 15 March, 15 May, 15 July, 15 September, 15 November, and 15 January of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or underpayment attracts a delinquency surcharge of 1% for every two days of delay, up to 15%, plus interest; the tax authority may seize bank accounts or business assets and, in extreme recurrent non-compliance, enforce closure and administrative dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting of shareholders (AGM), including approval of the board business report, annual financial statements, profit appropriation and/or loss absorption
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders in general meeting under the Taiwan Company Act; the minutes become part of the subsequent filing with the Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be convened within six months after fiscal year-end, i.e., by 30 June for a calendar-year company; practical planning positions the AGM after the corporate income tax filing on 31 May.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If the AGM is not held within the statutory six-month window, a shareholder may petition the court to order convocation; responsible directors may be fined NT$10,000–NT$50,000; chronic failure to conduct shareholder governance may be treated as corporate dysfunction and trigger administrative strike-off/dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Post-AGM company-registry filing of approved financial statements, profit distribution resolution, and any concurrent changes in responsible persons, capital, or articles of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs – Company Registration Office (central competent authority for corporate registration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the AGM (by 30 July at the latest if the AGM is held on 30 June); any concurrent change in directors, supervisor, shareholders or articles must also be registered within the applicable 15-day post-occurrence window under the Company Act.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to register changes means the changes cannot be relied upon against third parties; MOEA may impose fines on responsible persons for non-registration; continued failure to maintain current registered records or actual business operations can lead to administrative strike-off under Company Act Article 10.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory-register audit by the corporate secretary, including reconciliation of the share register, directors/supervisors register, charges register, minutes book, and principal-shareholder records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Board of Directors and company secretary acting as internal governance function; the registers are inspectable by shareholder members and subject to regulatory demand by MOEA, the tax administration, or other authorities.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least once every financial year, completed before the AGM date and certified no later than 31 December of each calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Missing, inaccurate, or incomplete statutory registers make the responsible person subject to administrative fines under the Company Act; shareholders have a legally enforceable inspection right; destruction or concealment of records can trigger criminal liability; systemic failure to maintain registers may contribute to a finding of corporate non-operation and administrative dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Company Act Article 22-1 Responsible Persons and Principal Shareholders (10%+ UBO) digital filing and annual confirmation certificate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) through the company commerce information system; MOEA Investment Commission if a foreign investor's approved scope or shareholding changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Initial filing at incorporation; updates must be made within 15 days after any change in responsible persons or principal shareholders; if no change occurs, perform and date the annual confirmation at the AGM date; foreign-investment share transfers must be applied for/ratified with the MOEA Investment Commission within the applicable 30-day reporting/application window.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or update Article 22-1 data can result in fines on the responsible person from NT$50,000 to NT$500,000, with repeated daily penalties for continuing default; the JV may also face suspension of foreign-investment privileges, remittance restrictions, and an adverse notation in the corporate credit/register record.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Taiwan-incorporated Sino-foreign JV is mandatory-audited by an independent certified public accountant (CPA) if: (1) paid-in capital equals or exceeds NT$30 million, about USD 1,000,000; (2) balance-sheet total assets exceed NT$100 million, about USD 3,200,000, annual operating revenue exceeds NT$100 million, or average headcount exceeds 100, where MOEA scale thresholds apply; (3) the company is a bank, credit cooperative, insurance, securities, futures, financial holding, or public company; or (4) the parent group, tax authority, banking counterparty, or foreign-investment approval imposes a consolidated IFRS audit or special-purpose audit. Below those thresholds, the JV may prepare unaudited financial statements under Taiwan enterprise GAAP, but the board must still approve them, submit them to shareholders, and retain them for seven years.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Public companies must apply IFRS as endorsed by the Financial Supervisory Commission. Non-public companies in Taiwan apply the Taiwan Enterprise Accounting Standard under the Business Entity Accounting Act, its Enforcement Rules, and the Company Act, with book-tax reconciliation under the Income Tax Act; for a Sino-foreign JV under foreign-investment approval, parallel high-quality records must be maintained to support the ultimate parent's IFRS consolidation and transfer-pricing documentation.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Taiwan does not require a separate blanket annual UBO franchise filing; the statutory rule is a registration obligation under Company Act Article 22-1 requiring the company to file responsible persons and principal shareholders (holding 10% or more of shares or capital) with MOEA at incorporation and within 15 days after any change. As a compliance protocol, the corporate secretary must still perform an annual confirmation at the AGM date, reconcile the internal register to the MOEA database, and record any unreported change. For any shareholding transfer by a foreign JV partner, a change report/ratification must also be made to the MOEA Investment Commission within the applicable 30-day reporting/application window, and the company registry update must be lodged within the 15-day window; the transfer cannot be recognized for voting or dividend remittance purposes until these filings are completed.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Pledged Shares and Major Shareholders (UBO supporting data)
Minute Book of Shareholders' Meetings and Board Meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 – 2,500 per year for a compliant registered office/agent and virtual office arrangement outside the central Taipei business district; USD 3,000 – 6,000 per year for a Taipei CBD registered office with meeting room and local corporate secretarial support.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Research and development (R&D) tax credit under Article 5 of the Industrial Innovation Act: a 15% credit on qualified R&D expenditures, capped at 30% of current-year tax liability (with a 5-year carryforward in designated cases); investment tax credits for smart machinery and 5G/telecom equipment (10%-15%); reduced rates in specific free-trade port zones; statutory exemption for certain government subsidies; a 5% surtax on undistributed earnings applies under Article 66-9 of the Income Tax Act.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Settlement Return (Form 15) filed through the Ministry of Finance Electronic Tax Filing System (e-Tax, https://tax.nat.gov.tw).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual settlement return plus quarterly provisional tax payments. The annual return is filed once per fiscal year; provisional tax payments are due each September (for calendar-year taxpayers).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual settlement return must be filed by the last day of the fifth month following fiscal year-end (e.g., 31 May for a 31 December year-end). Provisional tax payment is due by 30 September of the current tax year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Unified Business Tax Number (UBIN), legal name, registered address, tax classification, incorporation date and date of approval for the Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm the entity is a Taiwan-resident profit-seeking enterprise despite non-resident shareholders. Disclose the ultimate beneficial owner, especially any Mainland China investor, in the statutory shareholding annex. Ensure no unreported permanent establishment or branch exists in Taiwan.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year start/end dates, accounting basis (cash/accrual), inventory valuation method, and depreciation method.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture, the calendar year is mandatory. Non-resident investors must ensure that accrual accounting is used consistently and that transfer-pricing adjustments under the Corporate Income Tax Unfavorable Transfer Pricing Regulations are correctly reflected.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total net sales, service fees, remote desktop access subscription income, IoT telemetry software fees, and all revenue from Taiwan and foreign customers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All remote screen-sharing and IoT telemetry software revenue, including amounts collected through Stripe or Paddle payment rails, must be fully reported. Offshore-source sales remain taxable because the company is managed and controlled in Taiwan. Do not exclude revenue merely because the payment platform is outside Taiwan.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 (Cost of Goods Sold and Operating Expenses)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of services, cloud hosting charges, personnel costs, depreciation, R&D expenditures, royalties, and intercompany fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductible expenses must be supported by substantive invoices and contracts. Payments to a foreign parent or offshore affiliate for royalties or technical service fees will be disallowed under Article 43-1 of the Income Tax Act unless supported by an arm's-length transfer-pricing analysis and proof of actual IP use. Nondeductible related-party charges must be added back to taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest income, dividend income, foreign-exchange gains/losses, asset disposal gains/losses, and miscellaneous non-operating items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest received from offshore related parties must be priced at arm's length. Foreign dividend income can be offset by a foreign tax credit only if the foreign taxes are documented. Any payments to non-residents that fail the arm's-length test must be reported as constructive dividends or disallowed expenses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax-exempt government subsidies, tax-free capital gains under special legislation, and deferred income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Tax exemptions concerning the Industrial Innovation Act, SME Development Statute, or specific investment incentives must be separately itemized. A non-resident parent cannot convert Taiwan-sourced royalty income into tax-exempt revenue without a valid treaty claim and economic-substance review.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Eligible net operating losses (NOL) carried forward within the statutory limit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses properly declared and audited are deductible. The continuity-of-business test under Article 39 must be satisfied. Losses attributable to a non-resident branch cannot offset Taiwan-source income unless the branch is part of the same profit-seeking enterprise.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of taxable net income, application of the 20% statutory rate, alternative minimum tax (AMT) calculation, and surtax on undistributed earnings.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 20% profit-seeking enterprise income tax rate to the adjusted taxable income. If the joint venture retains profits that are not distributed, the 5% undistributed-earnings surtax under Article 66-9 must be separately calculated. Any profit distribution to non-residents triggers a separate 21% withholding tax on dividends.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credits, investment tax credits, withholding tax credits, and quarterly provisional tax payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Withholding tax paid by the company on behalf of a non-resident shareholder is creditable only if legally attributed to the company. Obtain foreign withholding certificates before claiming foreign tax credits. Provisional tax payments must be reconciled; a refund is available if credits exceed tax due.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 10 (Net Tax Due/Refund and Non-Resident Remittance Statement)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax payable or refund, and the schedule of undistributed earnings allocated to each non-resident shareholder.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: When remitting profits to a Mainland China or other non-resident shareholder, the withholding tax must be paid to the National Taxation Bureau by the tenth day of the month following distribution. Attach a Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial-ownership declaration if claiming treaty relief; otherwise the 21% statutory rate applies. Failure to report the remittance triggers penalty under Article 114.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: a 10% surcharge of the assessed tax (minimum NT$1,500, maximum NT$30,000) is imposed for failure to file by the statutory deadline. If the taxpayer fails to file after an extension notice, an additional 20% surcharge (minimum NT$15,000, maximum NT$30,000) applies. Late payment interest accrues at the Central Bank of China discount rate plus 5% per annum, compounded daily. Understatement or tax evasion: a penalty of up to twice the underpaid amount under Article 110 of the Income Tax Act, plus criminal liability under Article 41 of the Tax Collection Act (up to five years' imprisonment, detention, or a fine of up to NT$60,000). Directors may also be subject to a travel ban under Article 24 of the Tax Collection Act if the outstanding tax liability exceeds NT$10 million.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 21% on dividends distributed to non-resident shareholders; 0% withholding for resident corporate shareholders under the current single-rate imputation framework.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief (including the Cross-Strait Avoidance of Double Taxation Agreement signed in 2015, if applied, and all other Taiwan DTAs), the mandatory protocol is: (1) file the prescribed application form with the National Taxation Bureau of Taiwan (Form A-1/A-2 or the authority's equivalent); (2) attach the Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the investor's home country tax authority, apostilled/authenticated where applicable; (3) submit a Beneficial Ownership Statement with supporting organizational documents (shareholder register, board resolutions, funding agreements, audited financial statements) proving the recipient has economic substance; (4) demonstrate that the entity receiving the income is not a hybrid that creates double non-taxation; (5) obtain an advance approval before distribution where feasible, or apply for a refund within ten years; (6) if the TRC or beneficial-ownership proof is rejected, the statutory 21% dividend / 20% interest or royalty rate applies.

stage_6.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding rates: 20% for interest and 20% for royalties paid to non-residents (Income Tax Act Articles 88 and 92). Treaty rates: most Taiwan DTA partners receive a 10% maximum on interest and royalties. Under the Cross-Strait Agreement if effective, dividends, interest, and royalties may each be capped at 10%, subject to the same TRC and beneficial-ownership requirements. Note that certain interest categories (e.g., short-term commercial paper or bank deposits) are subject to a reduced 10-15% rate.
